# Implement block: Slingshot Send Money (React Native)

You are adding the "Slingshot Send Money" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A full-screen send-money confirmation with no cards: a vertical sheet of satin bands (dusty rose at the top, near-black brown behind the amount, a mauve band under the hint, red-brown at the bottom), the recipient's round picture with the initial "D" and the name "Dave" at the top, "$4.50" in white 64 pt bold at 37% of the height, the hint "SWIPE DOWN" in wide-spaced capitals at 58%, and a round close and a round pencil button in the bottom corners. Dragging down anywhere pulls the amount like the pouch of a slingshot: it trails the finger with ghost copies smearing behind it and leans as if it hung from the recipient, the hint follows less far, the bands stretch down and the top two thirds of the screen heat to amber in proportion to the pull; past the threshold the hint reads "RELEASE TO SEND" and the corner buttons fade out. Letting go there fires the amount up into the recipient, shrinking and fading with its ghosts behind it while the amber drains; a green disc with a white check then pops in where the amount was, with "Sent" under it and a "Done" pill rising from the bottom, and Done drops the amount back out of the picture. Letting go short of the threshold springs everything back.

**Motion.** Nothing is tied to the finger. A drag of (dx, dy) sets an aim: down by 0.8 × dy up to 24.5% of the screen's height, then with rubber-band resistance (at most 56 pt more), and sideways by 0.32 × dx (±46 pt). The amount is drawn four times, each copy chasing the aim on its own spring (mass 1; stiffness/damping 170/16 for the text, 118/13.5, 84/11.5 and 60/10 for its ghosts at 36%, 24% and 14% opacity); a ghost shows in proportion to how far it trails the aim, fully at 22 pt, so resting text is sharp and moving text smears. A copy that lags is strained: up to 24% taller and 7% narrower at 150 pt behind. Each copy is rotated by −x/420 rad. The hint has the same four copies on softer springs (110/14, 80/12, 58/10.5, 42/9) and travels 62% as far. Heat is the pull as a share of the travel on a spring (130/20): it mixes the 14 gradient colours from the satin palette to the amber one, moves their stops down, and fades in a radial amber glow (30%) under the recipient; the corner buttons fade out between 45% and 80% heat. At 72% of the travel the pull is armed: the hint's wordings cross-fade in 140 ms (white 60% to 90%) with a medium haptic, a light one when it falls back. Release when armed: the aim jumps to the recipient's picture, so the copies fly up on the same springs (about 0.25 s), shrinking to 40% and fading out between 30% and 72% of the way; the hint fades in 220 ms as it rises; the picture swells 10% at 150 ms (90 ms in, spring 260/12 out). 900 ms after the release the check disc pops from scale 0 (spring 260/15), the recipient fades out in 250 ms, the Done pill rises from below the screen (spring 190/19), and 120 ms later the check stroke draws in 220 ms as "Sent" fades in, with a success haptic. Done: check and label fade in 180 ms, the pill sinks in 260 ms (cubic ease-in), the recipient fades in over 250 ms, the amount springs back down from the picture with its ghosts, the corner buttons return after 260 ms and the hint after 320 ms over 350 ms. A release that is not armed puts the aim back to zero and the springs carry everything home with a small overshoot. The self-playing demo moves the same aim from a clock, period 9 s: a test pull to 42% from 0.8 s (0.5 s cubic ease-out) released at 1.45 s, a full pull from 2.3 s over 0.95 s (smoothstep) drifting 34 pt to the right, a hold in which the finger trembles by 2% (9 rad/s) and wanders to 34 pt left, the release at 4.3 s, Done pressed at 7.0 s for 150 ms, then rest; it gives no haptics, and a touch stops it until 3 s after the last touch, when it starts again from rest. Under reduced motion the springs jump (no lag, no ghosts, no strain), the amount fades out where it was let go instead of flying, and the check and the pill fade in instead of popping and rising.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [index.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/forms/slingshot-send-money/index.tsx)

### Files of the block

- [SlingshotSendMoney.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/forms/slingshot-send-money/SlingshotSendMoney.tsx)

### Packages

- `@expo/vector-icons`
- `@shopify/react-native-skia`
- `expo-haptics`
- `expo-status-bar`
- `react-native-gesture-handler`
- `react-native-reanimated`
- `react-native-safe-area-context`
- `react-native-worklets`

The versions the block was built with are in [react-native/package.json](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/package.json).

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
